ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the Cartesian coordinate system, the position of the square $ABCD$ is shown in the diagram, with the coordinates of point $A$ being $\left(1, 0\right)$ and the coordinates of point $D$ being $\left(0, 2\right)$. Extend $CB$ to meet the $x$-axis at point ${A}_{1}$, and construct the square ${A}_{1}{B}_{1}{C}_{1}C$; extend ${C}_{1}{B}_{1}$ to meet the $x$-axis at point ${A}_{2}$, and construct the square ${A}_{2}{B}_{2}{C}_{2}{C}_{1}$, and so on according to this pattern, what is the area of the 2021st square?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} \\
Let point A be (1,0), and point D be (0,2),\\
therefore, OA=1, OD=2, BC=AB=AD=$\sqrt{5}$,\\
considering squares ABCD and A$_{1}$B$_{1}$C$_{1}$C,\\
therefore, $\angle$OAD+$\angle$A$_{1}$AB=$90^\circ$, $\angle$ADO+$\angle$OAD=$90^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle$A$_{1}$AB=$\angle$ADO,\\
since $\angle$AOD=$\angle$A$_{1}$BA=$90^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\triangle$AOD $\sim$ $\triangle$A$_{1}$BA,\\
thus, $\frac{AO}{{A}_{1}B}=\frac{OD}{AB}$,\\
thus, $\frac{1}{{A}_{1}B}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}$,\\
therefore, ${A}_{1}B=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}$,\\
hence, ${A}_{1}{B}_{1}={A}_{1}C={A}_{1}B+BC=\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{5}$,\\
Similarly, it can be derived that, ${A}_{2}{B}_{2}=\frac{9}{4}\sqrt{5}=\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{2}\sqrt{5}$,\\
Similarly, it can be derived that, ${A}_{3}{B}_{3}=\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{3}\sqrt{5}$,\\
Similarly, it can be derived that, ${A}_{2020}{B}_{2020}=\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{2020}\sqrt{5}$,\\
Therefore, the area of the 2021st square is $\left[\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{2021−1}\times\sqrt{5}\right]^{2}=5\times\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{4040}$.\\
Hence, the answer is: $\boxed{5\times\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{4040}}$.
